findings.source: RenovaItem.sol:35 mint(address tokenOwner, uint256 hashverseItemId); event Mint(address indexed tokenOwner, uint256 tokenId, uint256 hashverseItemId); :21 initialize(...)
findings.issue: Parameter and event-field names come from unrelated contracts sharing the selector / topic: the hashverse item id is called '_amount' (and 'mintTokens' in the event), the minted token id 'mintAmount', and the initializer's arguments carry OHM staking names.
findings.rule: Same as the c00113 naming finding: use database parameter names only when unambiguous for the selector / topic, otherwise print _param1... (keep the function or event name).

notes: RenovaItem (ERC721 + royalties + Wormhole bridging), 30 functions, all reviewed: the ERC721 functions, mint (with _checkOnERC721Received), wormholeBridgeOut (0x258ad6ee: burn, nonce, publishMessage with value, events) and wormholeBridgeIn (0x7b0cad31: parseAndVerifyVM, emitter / chain checks, replay protection, _mintItem) by structure, the setters and getters in full; all correct. The pack has no source for 28 of the sections ('no source definition found in the AST', inherited functions); they were compared with contracts/nft and contracts/wormhole and the OpenZeppelin sources directly. Source loop: OpenZeppelin Strings.toString 'while (true)' (reached from tokenURI), shown rotated: the last digit is written before 'while t / 10:' (P3), after an inlined Math.log10 if-chain. The other whiles are copies (string concatenation in tokenURI, the VM struct decode and payload copies in wormholeBridgeIn: P7). RenovaItem's own sources have no loops.
summary: Faithful and complete; the single library loop is shown (rotated), and the main oddity is misleading parameter names from the signature database.
